data.source_title: Cost and clinical effectiveness of MRI in occult scaphoid fractures: a randomised controlled trial
data.locator: PubMed abstract; 84 ED patients randomized to early MRI or clinic reassessment.
data.source_setting: UK district general hospital ED; suspected occult scaphoid fracture; MRI arm early wrist MRI and discharge if no injury, control clinic reassessment.
data.source_period: Published 2013 (online 2012); recruitment dates not stated in abstract.
data.quantity: Mean clinic appointments during study follow-up
data.unit: clinic appointments per participant; mean ± SD
data.source_evidence_basis: Inspected PubMed abstract reports fewer mean clinic appointments in MRI group; it also reports scaphoid fracture 3/45 (6.7%) versus 4/39 (10.3%).
data.limitations: Small single-centre RCT; abstract does not supply a detailed follow-up duration for appointment count. Appointment burden is not probability of referral, failed follow-up, or return visit.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external pathway utilization comparator only. Do not infer that MRI causes fewer ED returns or that this rate transfers to local practice.
